messages:

Subject: Post-call: network acceptance items for private connectivity

Thanks for the call this morning — good discussion. To make sure our NetOps and security teams can scope the Private deployment, can you send over a concise acceptance matrix that covers the items we discussed? High-level asks:

- PrivateLink vs VPC peering recommendation and implications (route tables / ENI footprint)
- Precise egress/ingress IP ranges or a way to allowlist (we run a strict firewall)
- TLS / mutual TLS or cert expectation for control plane & data plane
- Log/audit endpoints (where do we push access logs and for how long)
- Expected maintenance windows and SLA escalation path

If you can include a short column that says "who owns" (HelixOne vs Redwood) for each item that would help our procurement and SRE teams. Ideally we want this by end-of-week to get our change window scheduled.

Thanks,
Alex

HelixOne

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-16T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: network acceptance items for private connectivity

Alex — thanks for the summary and the clear asks. I pulled together an initial acceptance matrix and attached two artifacts: redwood-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (matrix with ownership columns + example timelines) and network-egress-ranges.csv (sample egress CIDRs we use for hosted endpoints).

Quick summary (high level):
- Deployment mode recommendation: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) for HelixOne is the least invasive to your routing and the easiest to tie to allowlists. We still call out VPC peering as an alternative when customers want direct L3 routing and slightly lower hop counts; peering requires cross-account route changes and subnet IP planning.
- Egress/Allowlist: we can provide a stable set of egress IPs per-region (see CSV). If you run an internal proxy we can also support tunneling via a customer-controlled proxy (we’ll document health checks).
- TLS: redwood supports TLS 1.2+ for control and data planes; we recommend mTLS for the control plane (optional for data plane depending on your threat model).
- Logs & Retention: by default we retain audit traces for 90 days in the managed plane; for Private deployments we can forward logs to your CloudWatch/S3/GCS (configurable).

Next steps I propose:
1) Network deep-dive with your NetOps (60 min) — can you propose two times next week?
2) Confirm whether you prefer PrivateLink or Peering; if PrivateLink, provide the three subnets we should target for ENI placement and the account ID for our endpoint service allowlist.
3) If you need it, I’ll loop in our security lead for an evidence transfer and pen test scope.

I’ve flagged Karthik on the technical questions below — he added a short tech appendix for NetOps.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood-acceptance-matrix.xlsx (xlsx), network-egress-ranges.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@helixone.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-17T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: network acceptance items for private connectivity — technical appendix

Alex / team — following Neha's note, a few technical specifics from the serving/runtime perspective that will speed the NetOps call: 

1) Ports & protocols
 - TLS (443) for model API traffic; control plane uses 443 as well (mTLS supported on 8443 if you prefer separate port).
 - Health probes: TCP/HTTP 443 from Redwood-managed monitoring IP ranges (see CSV).

2) PrivateLink vs Peering (practical differences)
 - PrivateLink (recommended for strict firewall/allowlist workflows): creates interface endpoints in three customer subnets (ENIs). Advantage: you only need to allow ENI IPs in your firewall and no route table changes cross-account. Drawbacks: slightly more ENI management and potential for quota increases on your side.
 - VPC Peering: lower network hop and no ENI; requires route table updates and careful CIDR non-overlap. If HelixOne wants full L3 routing between VPCs and expects very large intra-VPC traffic volumes, peering can be attractive.
 - NATTing/Egress model: If your VPC uses a centralized NAT/proxy, we can egress through that path — provide proxy host and health-check endpoints.

3) Sample egress CIDRs (from our CSV)
 - us-east-1: 34.200.128.0/20, 34.201.64.0/20
 - us-west-2: 44.208.0.0/20
 - note: we can provide per-deployment sticky egress IPs for Dedicated/Private installs if you require immutable allowlists.

4) Certificates & auth
 - For PrivateLink we will present our server cert; if you require mTLS we will provide a CSR flow or accept your client certs.

5) Ownership matrix (quick):
 - Subnet provisioning: HelixOne
 - Route table changes (peering): HelixOne
 - ENI quotas & PrivateLink setup: Redwood (coord) / HelixOne approve
 - Audit log forwarding: HelixOne (config) / Redwood (push)

I attached a short checklist in the redwood-acceptance-matrix.xlsx under the "technical" tab. If you can confirm: (a) preferred connectivity mode, (b) three subnets for ENIs (w/ AZ), and (c) contact for service-account IAM role creation (if you want the tighter cross-account setup), we’ll draft the exact runbook for the NetOps change window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
